findings.claim: The merge commit ae7f8fa dropped the PR's voidVisit handling, on the strength of a Javadoc claim that VisitWithQueueEntriesSaveHandler already voids entries on the voidVisit path. That handler's void branch only fires when core's BaseVoidHandler has already run, and the order between them is a HashMap tie-break, so the ticket's actual symptom (deleting a visit, i.e. REST DELETE /visit/{uuid} -> voidVisit) is still not reliably fixed.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, deleting a visit on any deployment where VisitWithQueueEntriesSaveHandler iterates before BaseVoidHandler (the ticket reports this is the case on the Reference Application) voids the visit but leaves its queue entries active, so the patient stays in the service queue. That is exactly O3-5459, and it fails silently with no exception. Fix: add a dedicated VisitWithQueueEntriesVoidHandler that voids the entries from the handle() args (voidingUser/voidedDate/voidReason), mirroring PatientWithQueueEntriesVoidHandler, and drop VoidHandler from the save handler. The alternative is to restore the voidVisit branch the merge removed.
findings.evidence: git show ae7f8fa / git diff 36b2040 ae7f8fa -- VisitWithQueueEntriesDeleteAdvice.java: the merge removes the `if ("voidVisit".equals(...))` branch and adds the purge-only guard at line 41 plus the 'Voiding needs no advice' Javadoc (lines 30-33). VisitWithQueueEntriesSaveHandler.java:62 guards on `visit.getVoided()`. Core 2.7.4: VisitServiceImpl.voidVisit is just dao.saveVisit, so the work is done by RequiredDataAdvice's void branch -> HandlerUtil.getHandlersForType(VoidHandler, Visit). That method sorts by @Handler order, and BaseVoidHandler, VisitVoidHandler and the queue handler all have the default Integer.MAX_VALUE, so the tie keeps the iteration order of ServiceContext.getRegisteredComponents, which is `new HashMap<>(getBeansOfType(...))` keyed by bean name. REST VisitResource1_9.delete calls voidVisit. I ran a scratch integration test (deleted afterwards) under JDK 8 with `mvn -o -pl integration-tests -am -Dtest=ZzProbeTest,...`. (a) Default test-context order [BaseVoidHandler, VisitWithQueueEntriesSaveHandler, VisitVoidHandler]: voidVisit -> entryVoided=true (known-good control). (b) Same cached handler list with the queue handler moved first: visitVoided=true, entryVoided=false (known-bad). (c) The real 7 VoidHandler bean names copied into java.util.HashMap exactly as ServiceContext does, plus N synthetic names: baseBeforeQueue=true up to 23 beans and false from 24 on (the table resize), so the relative order depends on which modules are installed. The PR head itself (O3-5955) adds patientWithQueueEntriesVoidHandler to that set. VisitWithQueueEntriesSaveHandlerTest:122 states in a comment that the outcome 'depends on it running after core's BaseVoidHandler, so pin the outcome', but the pin only holds for the test context's bean set. Dennis Kigen's 2026-07-03 ticket comment gives the same root cause and reports the failure on RefApp.

findings.claim: The PR title and description still say the advice intercepts voidVisit and that void and purge are both tested, and the ticket's 'verified live, approved' comment was written against that earlier version. At this head the advice is purge-only and no test in the diff exercises voiding.
findings.evidence: Read pr96-body-at-round1.md ('voidVisit(): voids all associated queue entries', 'Added tests for both void and purge scenarios'). The ticket comment (2026-07-03) describes the fix as hooking voidVisit and purgeVisit. git diff main...HEAD: the advice returns early unless the method is purgeVisit (line 41), and VisitWithQueueEntriesDeleteAdviceTest contains only two purge tests. The 39195a0 -> 36b2040 commits did carry a void path and a void test, which the merge removed.

verdict: Not ready to merge. The purge half is correct and tested, but the merge commit removed the voidVisit fix, so visit deletion (the ticket's symptom) still depends on a HashMap tie-break between VoidHandlers and is reported to fail on the Reference Application.
what_i_swept: Checked the diff stat (3 files, +170/-0, identical for main...HEAD and main HEAD). Read the PR body, O3-5459 with its comments, and O3-5461. Read the full advice, its test, and config.xml. Walked the commit stack and diffed the merge commit's changes to the PR files (36b2040..ae7f8fa), which is how the dropped voidVisit branch surfaced. Solution fit: traced the ticket's delete path through REST VisitResource1_9.delete -> VisitService.voidVisit -> core 2.7.4 RequiredDataAdvice void branch -> HandlerUtil ordering -> ServiceContext.getRegisteredComponents HashMap, then drove it in a scratch test with control and swapped orders. Compared against the sibling PatientWithQueueEntriesVoidHandler (order-independent, uses the handle() args). Purge: confirmed a bare purgeVisit without the advice fails with ConstraintViolationException, so the PR's purge tests are real regressions, and they pass at head. Confirmed RequiredDataAdvice has no purge branch (Javadoc claim holds), and found no self or other FK onto queue_entry since visit_queue_entries was dropped in liquibase. Outward trace: TransactionProxyFactoryBean chain (preInterceptors incl. AuthorizationAdvice, then TransactionInterceptor), with Context.addAdvice appending after it, so the advice runs after the privilege check and inside the transaction, and the Visit.purge.inUse exception rolls back the entry deletes. ModuleFileParser 2.7.4 does not validate config.xml against the DTD, so the <advice> placement is safe. Proxy-privilege handling matches the existing handlers. Security, performance and conventions: nothing beyond the above.
could_not_verify: I did not run the Reference Application. That handler order actually flips there comes from the ticket comment (observed on core 2.8.7 / queue 3.0.0 with the same `visit.getVoided()` guard), not from my own run. My HashMap probe used the real test-context bean names plus synthetic names, so it shows the order depends on the deployment's bean set, not the exact RefApp threshold.

I did not build the base branch to run the PR's purge test there (the advice class does not exist on base). The bare-purge probe stands in for it: without the advice, purgeVisit fails on the queue_entry FK.
notes: Pass 1 (diff, ticket, commit stack, void-path trace with probe) found F1. Pass 2 (transaction/authorization ordering, config DTD, FK graph, REST purge/delete, sibling handler) found only F2. Pass 3 (test coverage and Javadoc claims re-read against core) found nothing new. The 'Voiding needs no advice' Javadoc and the 'pin the outcome' test comment in main contradict each other: the test comment admits the order dependency the Javadoc denies. The scratch probe file ZzProbeTest.java was deleted, and `git status --porcelain` is clean.
